To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ethical decision-making process of university students in an international business context is not as straightforward as it may seem.
ethical decisions in the international business environment are made by university students based on their own ethical judgment and motivation.
students’ ethical decision-making is influenced by their own moral judgment and their intention to make ethical decisions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model to explain how students make ethical decisions in international business and to suggest a new approach to teaching business ethics in universities.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the teaching of ethical decision-making should be a part of the business curriculum, and it should be taught as a process of ethical decision-making, not as a product.
the teaching of business ethics should focus on stimulating the intention (motivations) of students to make ethical decisions.
the teaching and learning of ethical decision-making should not be a simple and straightforward process, but rather a challenging and complex one.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the teaching of business ethics needs to focus on the motivation to initiate an ethical decision.
we should not just teach business students how to make ethical decisions, but also how to motivate them to do so in real life.
the teaching of ethical decision-making should be based upon a clear understanding of the four components of moral decision-making.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ethical decision-making in the international business setting should not be taught in isolation from the business curriculum but should instead be integrated into it.
the teaching of ethics should be more practical and realistic in order to help future global talents make ethical decisions in real-life situations.
the current teaching of business ethics in business schools does not adequately prepare the next generation of managers to deal with the ethical challenges they will face.
